probes.summary: Nginx configuration and service are healthy; node2 completed SNI TLS and received the declared health response.
The served certificate is valid for node1 for one year, self-issued, self-verifying, and matches Nginx’s configured certificate.
The existing HTTPS root content and health response remain unchanged.
Both preparation-owned continuity and availability probes remain active with live processes.
Operational TLS checks passed, but stale legacy TLS material and failed ssh.service units remain.

assertions.summary: Nginx is valid, enabled, active, TLS-capable with SNI node1, and /healthz returns the required response.

evidence.observation: exit_code=0; nginx.conf syntax is ok and configuration test is successful.

evidence.command: systemctl is-enabled nginx; systemctl is-active nginx

evidence.observation: exit_code=0; CONNECTION ESTABLISHED; TLSv1.3; Peer certificate: CN=node1; Verification: OK.

assertions.summary: The served certificate matches node1, is currently valid with at least 180 days remaining, is self-issued, and verifies successfully.

evidence.command: openssl s_client -connect node1:443 -servername node1 -showcerts < /dev/null 2>/dev/null | openssl x509 -noout -subject -issuer -dates -fingerprint -sha256 -ext subjectAltName -checkhost node1 -checkend 15552000
evidence.observation: exit_code=0; subject=CN=node1; issuer=CN=node1; notAfter=Aug 26 18:49:24 2027 GMT; SAN DNS:node1; SHA-256 fingerprint 95:EC:DA:B5:04:C5:FC:CC:4B:7C:7D:E8:E4:00:EA:9E:77:B9:06:AD:79:67:6F:D3:57:B6:02:D9:F0:10:78:D8; Certificate will not expire.
exit_code=0; Peer certificate CN=node1; Verification: OK.

assertions.summary: The served and effective configured certificates have the same SHA-256 fingerprint.

evidence.command: openssl s_client -connect node1:443 -servername node1 -showcerts < /dev/null 2>/dev/null | openssl x509 -noout -subject -issuer -dates -fingerprint -sha256 -ext subjectAltName -checkhost node1 -checkend 15552000

evidence.observation: exit_code=0; stdout: existing HTTPS content: preserve during certificate rotation.

assertions.summary: Both preparation-owned probes are active with nonzero live processes: the long-lived continuity transfer and rapid health loop.

evidence.command: for u in infraset-continuity.service infraset-availability.service; do printf '[%s]\n' "$u"; systemctl is-active "$u"; pid=$(systemctl show "$u" -p MainPID --value); systemctl show "$u" -p ActiveState -p SubState -p MainPID; ps -p "$pid" -o pid=,stat=,etime=,args=; done
evidence.observation: Both units report active/running. infraset-continuity has MainPID 1346 running curl against https://node1/continuity.bin; infraset-availability has MainPID 1347 running the repeating health loop.

ssh.service is reported failed on both managed nodes; the authored clean-state assertion includes concrete failed units.

actions_performed: Executed only read-only managed-cluster checks on node1 and node2 in authored probe order.
No mutation, recovery, or evaluator cleanup action was performed; all probes are marked cleanup_completed=true.
Called complete_evidence exactly once after all live checks.
overall_summary: Operational TLS, content preservation, certificate validity, certificate matching, and continuity assertions passed. tls-state-clean failed because the expired legacy certificate and extra legacy private key remain, and ssh.service is failed on both nodes.
